text:
Acme Ops: hey @support — after we switched Acme-Prod to the interface endpoint (aws vpce) we started seeing intermittent 503s and occasional TLS handshake failures to api.redwood.com. Started ~09:12 UTC. We flipped private DNS on when creating the endpoint.

Acme Ops: quick repro outputs below (sanitized):
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com
34.198.12.45   ; public ELB IP (sometimes)
vpce-0a1b2c3d-abcdef.elb.amazonaws.com. ; sometimes returns this CNAME

$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 34.198.12.45 (34.198.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca

# other times we get HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable from the same IP
```

Amy (Support): thanks — can you paste the VPC endpoint id, the subnets it's attached to, and whether you enabled "Private DNS" on the interface endpoint? also any Route53 outbound rules or resolver endpoints?

Acme Ops: vpce-0a1b2c3d, subnets: subnet-aaa, subnet-bbb, private DNS was enabled. we have an inbound resolver endpoint for cross-account DNS (resolves internal hostnames to another account). No custom NAT changes.

Jordan (SE): likely suspects in order: split-horizon DNS + resolver hops, endpoint SG/NACL egress, or TLS being terminated by a public ELB when traffic escapes the VPC. Two quick checks to prioritize: 
1) from an EC2 in the same subnet as your app, run `dig +short api.redwood.com @169.254.169.253` (or the VPC resolver IP) and compare to from the app pod. we want to confirm the same resolver and that the name resolves to the interface endpoint ENI IPs (10.x.x.x) not public ALB IPs.
2) run `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.com -alpn h2` against the returned IP to inspect cert subject/SNI. the error you pasted looks like the cert chain is not what we expect (unknown ca) or SNI was stripped/proxied.

Infra Oncall Bot: cc @infra-oncall — tagging because cross-VPC resolver + conditional forwarders frequently cause mixed answers (public vs private) and intermittent 503s if some app nodes hit the public path.

Acme Ops: ran the dig from a pod and from EC2: pod -> 34.198.12.45, EC2 -> 10.3.45.12 (ENI of vpce). So pod DNS is still resolving to public IP. We use kube-dns + outbound UDP traffic to a corporate resolver that forwards to Route53.

Jordan (SE): that matches split-horizon/resolver forwarding mismatch. common root causes:
- kubelet/resolver is pointed at corporate forwarder which forwards public queries to internet instead of the VPC resolver (conditional forwarders missing).
- the VPC interface endpoint's private DNS only applies to the VPC resolver; any external forwarder that isn't configured for the VPC private zone will return public records.

Jordan (SE): quick mitigation options:
- configure the cluster DNS to query the VPC resolver first (169.254.169.253 on AWS) or create a conditional forwarder on your corporate resolver for `api.redwood.com` pointing to the VPC resolver IP(s).
- as a short-lived workaround, add an allowlist to your NAT/egress policy to force traffic to the VPCE ENI IP range (not ideal).

Amy (Support): also re: TLS: if some requests land on the public ELB, the ALB hostname/cert may not include the private service name used on the interface endpoint; that will produce cert validation errors or 'unknown ca' if there's client cert expectations. After DNS fix you should see consistent ENI IPs and the cert should match.

Acme Ops: we don't control the corporate resolver, ops team says they can't forward per-hostname. any low-friction switch?

Jordan (SE): deployment-wise:
- confirm the VPCE's security group allows inbound 443 from your app subnets and allows outbound to Redwood's backends (if you're using egress allowlisting).
- check NACLs for ephemeral port return traffic (TCP 1024-65535) — NACL denies can break TLS handshake if return ports blocked.
- pod DNS config: `cat /etc/resolv.conf` inside a failing pod and share. often pods use `ndots` that cause queries to go to upstream resolver in different order.

Acme Ops: pasted resolv.conf (sanitized):
```
nameserver 10.10.10.10  # corporate resolver
search corp.local
options ndots:5 timeout:2
```

Jordan (SE): yep that's the issue: corporate resolver is first. If it cannot forward to the VPC resolver for that name you get the internet answer. Two paths: 1) change pod resolv order so the VPC resolver is hit first (policy-based) or 2) create a Route53 inbound endpoint and let corporate resolver forward `api.redwood.com` to it.

Acme Ops: what about the TLS unknown ca message? we use our own root CAs for mutual TLS with some partners — could that interfere?

Amy (Support): the unknown ca in your curl output is coming from the server side during handshake (client sees alert from server). That usually means the client and server couldn't agree on a cert chain or SNI didn't match and the server aborted. Once DNS is consistent we should retest. If you still see TLS alerts after DNS resolves to the ENI IPs, capture `openssl s_client -connect 10.3.45.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts` and share the leaf cert subject and issuer.

Infra Oncall Bot: next steps checklist: 
- [ ] change/test pod DNS ordering to prefer VPC resolver (or add conditional forwarder)
- [ ] validate VPCE SGs allow app subnet -> port 443 and return ephemeral ports
- [ ] check NACLs for no egress deny on 1024-65535
- [ ] run `openssl s_client` against ENI IP to confirm cert

Acme Ops: will try DNS order change first and report back. If we can't change corporate resolver soon, we'll spin a short-lived sidecar that resolves via VPC resolver and proxies traffic. thanks team :thumbsup:

Amy (Support): +1, and if you hit lingering 503s after dns fix tag this thread and include the `openssl` output and a failing `curl -v` log. we'll escalate to infra/serving runtime for deeper path/tracing.

Acme Ops: update — changing cluster CoreDNS to forward `api.redwood.com` to 169.254.169.253 fixed the resolution; all traffic now hits VPCE ENI IPs and 503s dropped. still validating TLS errors but so far so good.

Jordan (SE): great. if TLS errors persist after a few minutes (conn pools and DNS caches clear) run the s_client check, but sounds like the resolver mismatch was the main culprit. closing loop once tidy.

Acme Ops: will close once we've run full smoke for 2 hours. thanks everyone!
